title: Lens Flare with Light Source Tracking
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a dynamic lens flare post-processing effect with real-time light source tracking.

SCENE SETUP:
- Create a dark space scene with a black background (0x000000).
- Use a PerspectiveCamera with FOV 60, near 0.1, far 2000, positioned at (0, 5, 30).
- Add OrbitControls for camera rotation (no zoom, no pan — only rotation).
- Place a large SphereGeometry (radius 500) with an inside-facing dark starfield material as the skybox.
- Scatter 200 small white IcosahedronGeometry stars (radius 0.1) randomly within a sphere of radius 300.

LIGHT SOURCES (3 total):
- Sun: A bright yellow PointLight (0xFFDD44, intensity 2) at position (50, 20, -60) with a visible yellow sphere mesh (radius 2, emissive 0xFFDD44).
- Blue Star: A blue PointLight (0x4488FF, intensity 1.5) at position (-40, 30, -80) with a visible blue sphere mesh (radius 1.5, emissive 0x4488FF).
- Red Dwarf: A red PointLight (0xFF4422, intensity 1) at position (20, -15, -50) with a visible red sphere mesh (radius 1, emissive 0xFF4422).

LENS FLARE SYSTEM:
- Implement a custom lens flare system using screen-space calculations (do NOT use the deprecated Three.js Lensflare addon — build it from scratch).
- For each light source, project its world position to screen coordinates (NDC) every frame.
- For each light, generate 5 flare elements: a main glow at the light's screen position, and 4 secondary flare ghosts placed along the line from the light's screen position through the screen center, at distances 0.3, 0.6, 0.9, and 1.2 times the vector from light to center.
- Each flare element is a screen-space quad (use a separate overlay Scene + OrthographicCamera, or DOM overlay divs with CSS). Use circular gradient textures generated via canvas (radial gradient from white/color center to transparent edge).
- Main glow size: 80px, ghost sizes: 50px, 35px, 25px, 18px. Scale all sizes by the light's intensity.
- Flare opacity should be modulated by: (a) the dot product between camera forward vector and the vector from camera to light (flare fades as light moves to screen edge), and (b) an occlusion check — cast a Raycaster from camera toward each light; if any mesh is hit before the light distance, that light's flare opacity drops to 0.

ACTIVE LIGHT SELECTION & CONTROLS:
- Maintain an 'activeLight' index (0=Sun, 1=BlueStar, 2=RedDwarf).
- Press keys 1, 2, 3 to select the active light.
- Press I/K to increase/decrease the active light's intensity by 0.25 (clamp to [0, 3]).
- Press O to toggle occlusion checking on/off globally.
- Press F to toggle the entire flare system on/off.
- Press R to reset all lights to their original intensities and positions.

ANIMATION:
- The Sun orbits slowly around the Y-axis at radius 78 (angular speed 0.1 rad/s).
- The Blue Star bobs up and down sinusoidally (amplitude 15, frequency 0.3 Hz) around its base Y.
- The Red Dwarf remains stationary.

HUD (top-left, white text on semi-transparent black background, monospace font):
- Line 1: 'Active: Sun|BlueStar|RedDwarf'
- Line 2: 'Intensity: X.XX'
- Line 3: 'Flares: ON|OFF'
- Line 4: 'Occlusion: ON|OFF'
- Line 5: 'Visible Lights: N/3'
- Line 6: 'FPS: XX'

STATE MANAGEMENT — expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
{
  activeLight: 0|1|2,
  lightIntensities: [sunI, blueI, redI],           // current intensities
  lightScreenPositions: [[nx,ny],[nx,ny],[nx,ny]],  // NDC coords [-1,1]
  lightVisible: [bool, bool, bool],                 // true if not occluded AND on screen
  flareEnabled: true|false,
  occlusionEnabled: true|false,
  flareElementCount: number,                        // total rendered flare elements this frame
  sunAngle: number,                                 // current orbit angle in radians
  blueStarY: number,                                // current Y position of blue star
  cameraPosition: {x,y,z},
  cameraTarget: {x,y,z},
  fps: number,
  lightWorldPositions: [[x,y,z],[x,y,z],[x,y,z]]
}

ENSURE:
- Smooth 60fps animation loop.
- All flare elements update positions every frame based on camera orientation.
- Flare ghosts correctly mirror through screen center.
- No NaN values in any state fields.
- The scene is fully self-contained in one HTML file with no external assets.
physics_constraints: Lens flare elements must be positioned along the line from each light's screen projection through the screen center. Occlusion raycasting must correctly hide flares when geometry blocks line of sight. Light intensity clamped to [0, 3]. Sun orbit radius fixed at 78 units. Blue star oscillation amplitude 15 units. Flare opacity proportional to dot product of camera forward and camera-to-light direction.
